defect: integrity_review paired the i-th point-start with the i-th point-terminal and refused any difference. That holds only when points are observed strictly one at a time. Concurrency inside a lane -- which observe_point permits, because it enforces order per lane and not per point -- makes terminals land in completion order, so 142 of 208 pairings differed while nothing was actually wrong.
fix: The check now verifies the relation instead of the position: no point starts twice, no point terminates twice, every terminal is preceded by its own start, and -- new -- the lanes appear in the order the field froze, which the positional check never looked at. It is strictly stronger than what it replaced, not merely more permissive, and the tests demonstrate that by rejecting three things the old check would have missed or never examined.
found_at_phase: after the sealed observation completed, before the leaderboard was compiled
found_by: the check refusing the completed observation
prevention: A concurrency decision should be checked against every consumer of the artifact it changes, not only the producer. The next edition should either state sequential observation as a requirement or verify the relation from the start; the positional form encoded an assumption it never declared.
rejected_alternatives: Reordering the journal to satisfy the check was rejected outright: that is forging the evidence the edition exists to produce. Re-running the observation sequentially is impossible without destroying a one-shot record, and would have cost fifteen hours to reproduce results that are already correct.
root_cause_is_mine: I chose to observe six points concurrently within a lane and verified that decision against observe_point's order rule and against append_record's locking. I did not check what integrity_review required of the finished journal. Checking how a value is consumed at one site and not at every site is the same mistake this edition has recorded repeatedly.
title: integrity review paired points by position, which assumes sequential observation
verified_before_changing_anything: Every property the positional check stood in for was confirmed to hold on the finished journal, independently and before the check was touched: each of the 208 points started exactly once and terminated exactly once; the terminal set equals the frozen field exactly; every terminal is preceded in the journal by its own start; and the twelve lanes were started contiguously in the frozen key-derived order. All 208 terminals are 'succeeded'. The 142 differences are entirely within-lane completion ordering.
why_this_is_not_a_retroactive_rule_chang: C19 forbids scoring, qualification and execution changes after the first sealed read. This is none of those. It changes no score, no cell, no rank, no eligibility verdict and no winner rule; it is a journal-mechanics assertion in the integrity review. The results remain unread at the time of this amendment -- observation is silent by construction, and no leaderboard has been compiled -- so the change cannot have been made to favour any outcome. That the change was made after seeing the check fail is recorded here plainly rather than left to be inferred.
